reason: Prioritize the one-entry panel loop: the supplied feasibility review supports its pointer and scratch mapping, and it avoids the measured sixteen-call wrapper’s repeated SME transitions. The three proposals for it are substantially the same experiment, so test only one implementation. The three 256-iteration two-K proposals also substantially overlap; test only one after confirming the current loop body matches the stated two-K form. Scratch lifetime and B-panel packing require coordinated traversal and pointer changes, with unverified benefits. Fused packing changes the long assembly body and has higher correctness risk. A-transpose requires a new generated shape that is not available to the implementation agent. Historical scores do not establish a winner or a cause.
